item.text:
**Bottom Line**
Kishida’s 2024 record is **mostly positive** on `5B.3`: he respected BOJ independence, treated fiscal soundness as a longer-run objective after restoring growth, and repeatedly framed policy around wage-led demand and investment. The main negatives are that inflation/yen weakness remained acute and political scandal made fiscal politics look defensive at times.

1. **Press Conference on the Bank of Japan Terminating Its Negative Interest Rate Policy** | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | March 19, 2024 | https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202403/19kaiken.html | Kishida said the BOJ had confirmed a sustainable price-wage virtuous cycle, that the accommodative environment could remain in place, that the government was **not** revising the 2013 accord, and that there was no noteworthy FX discussion. This is direct evidence for monetary credibility and central-bank independence. `5B.3`
2. **Policy Speech to the 213th Session of the Diet** | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | January 30, 2024 | https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202401/30shiseihoshin.html | He said the economy is the foundation of public finances, that Japan should first restore wage-led growth, and then move steadily toward fiscal soundness while continuing expenditure reform. This is strong evidence for fiscal responsibility and a long-term macro framework. `5B.3`, `5B.1`
3. **Press Conference by Prime Minister Kishida** | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | March 28, 2024 | https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202403/28kaiken.html | After budget enactment and tax-code revision, Kishida stressed reserve-budget use for the Noto response, incomes surpassing price increases, and continued close cooperation with the BOJ after its policy shift. This supports macro stabilization, though it also shows reliance on short-term relief tools. `5B.3`, `5B.1`
4. **Speech at the Keidanren Summer Forum 2024** | Prime Minister’s Office of Japan | July 19, 2024 | https://japan.kantei.go.jp/101_kishida/statement/202407/19forum.html | Kishida framed the June policy package as part of an irreversible transition from deflation to growth and said monetary normalization would help that transition. This is positive evidence for long-term investment conditions and monetary credibility. `5B.3`, `5B.1`
5. **Embattled Japan PM faces ethics committee to save popularity and budget** | Reuters | February 28, 2024 | https://www.investing.com/news/economy/embattled-japan-pm-faces-ethics-committee-to-save-popularity-and-budget-3319362 | Reuters reported the funding scandal forced Kishida into defensive politics around popularity and the budget. This is mixed negative evidence: short-term political survival pressures were affecting fiscal politics. `5B.3`, `5B.1`, `4B.10`
6. **Japan’s Kishida championed ‘new capitalism’ but was undone by yen** | Reuters | August 14, 2024 | https://www.thestar.com.my/news/world/2024/08/14/analysis-japan039s-kishida-championed-039new-capitalism039-but-was-undone-by-yen | Reuters noted Kishida pushed some of Japan’s biggest wage increases in decades, but the weak yen, higher prices, and scandals outweighed those gains politically. This is mixed evidence: macro improvement existed, but stability was incomplete and politically fragile. `5B.3`, `5B.1`, `4B.10`

**Search Gap**
I did not find credible evidence that Kishida directly undermined BOJ independence or caused a major fiscal blowout in 2024. The negative evidence is mostly about persistent inflation/yen weakness and the political scandal’s effect on budget politics, not explicit macroeconomic sabotage.
